business: Moduo: an all-in-one workspace, pitched as a time-blocking planner built around finishing what you schedule
by_segment: Employee at a startup or remote company
why_not: The 'no wall of red' part actually gets me, so I'd grab the free plan and play with it for a week, but I've done that with Sunsama and Akiflow and I always drift back to just Google Calendar. I'm not putting $12 a month on another planner until it survives past the novelty phase.

Honestly the 'no wall of red' bit is the first planner pitch that's spoken to me, so I'd grab the free plan or the no-card trial. But I just cancelled a $20 planner, I know my pattern: two great weeks, then I stop opening it, so I'm not paying anything in month one.

I just cancelled a $20 planner because it never really sat on top of my work calendar, and this pitch doesn't say a word about Google or Outlook sync. I might poke at the free plan, but I'm not paying for a new app with zero Reddit threads or YouTube comparisons against Sunsama or Akiflow.

The done/push/shrink/drop prompt is exactly the moment my plan dies at 11am, so I'd try the free plan, but nothing here says it syncs two ways with my work Google/Outlook calendar or has keyboard shortcuts and integrations. The done/push/shrink/drop thing is honestly my 11am problem, so I'd sign up for the free plan and maybe try the trial. But I wouldn't pay $12 a month in the first month; I'd sit on the free tier and see if I actually keep using it past week two like every other planner I've tried.

I just cancelled a $20 planner, and half the reason I time-block is checking the plan between meetings and on the go. Without a phone app this would only cover part of my day, and there are no reviews or Reddit threads yet to tell me it beats what I already tried.
flip: If after the trial I'm still opening it daily without forcing myself and it pulls in both my work Google and personal iCloud calendars, I'd pay.
